blocks.notes: Elbows locked, load taken slowly. If the inner elbow is already sore before you start, that is the session telling you to skip its straight-arm work.
blocks.intensity: light — this is preparation, not training
blocks.progression: Unchanged for the whole plan. It is the price of straight-arm work, not a thing to progress.

blocks.notes: Move the shoulder blade, not the elbow.

Nothing logged on this movement yet, so the numbers here are the rung's own standard rather than yours: treat the first session as finding out. Work up to one honest effort, log it, and everything after it scales from a real number. The volume stays deliberately below what you could probably do — new tissue load is where straight-arm injuries come from, not the set that felt hard. Hardest thing first, while you are completely fresh, and deliberately few sets of it. Stop the moment the shape is not there — this block is a look at the next position, not a fight with it.
blocks.intensity: about 55% of your best hold (5s) (estimated from the rung's own standard — nothing logged or declared for this yet)
blocks.progression: This is the rung above the one you are training. It moves when the rung below it does.

blocks.notes: Stop the set the moment the shape breaks, not when the arms give out. Several clean efforts beat one taken to collapse — a position held to failure rehearses the failure.
blocks.progression: Next week: one more second on every set, at the same quality. The hold is trained past 20s, not extended by sagging into it.

body.cooldown: Two minutes of easy shoulder extension and light elbow flexion. Straight-arm work is the one thing this app will not let you skip the after-care on.

phases.label: Joint Warm Up
phases.note: Every joint the session will load, taken through its range unloaded. Slow, and never into pain.

phases.label: Muscular Warm Up
phases.note: Raise temperature and blood flow. You should be warm and slightly out of breath before anything hard.

phases.label: Mobility / Dynamic Stretching
phases.note: Moving through range, not holding an end position. Long static holds before training cost strength for the next hour.

phases.label: Specific Warm-Up
phases.note: The movements of this session, at a fraction of the effort. This is rehearsal and potentiation, not training.

phases.label: Training
phases.note: The session itself, in the order it is written: skill and straight-arm work while fresh, then strength, then the rest.

phases.label: Cooldown
phases.note: Bring the breathing down and move gently through what was worked.

protocols.title: Joints, unloaded
steps: Ankles, knees and hips: 10 slow circles each, from the ground up.
Spine: 10 cat-cows, then 10 seated rotations each way.
Shoulders: 10 slow circles back, 10 forward, arms long.
Elbows: 10 full flexions and extensions, then 10 rotations of the forearm.
Wrists: 10 circles each way, then 10 slow flexions and extensions per hand.
protocols.see_clinician: A joint that is painful before it has been loaded at all is not a warm-up problem.

protocols.title: Raise
steps: Five minutes of easy cardio — skipping, rowing, a brisk walk — until you are warm and slightly out of breath.
Push-ups at half effort: 2 sets of 10.
Rows or an active hang at half effort: 2 sets of 10.

protocols.title: Mobilise
steps: Band or stick dislocates: 2 sets of 10, straight arms, as wide as you need.
Wall slides: 2 sets of 10, ribs down.
Deep squat, 5 slow rocks side to side, then stand and repeat once.
Leg swings, front to back and across: 10 each way per leg.
Thoracic rotations on all fours: 8 per side.

protocols.title: Straight-arm and elbow preparation
steps: Scapular pull-ups: 2 sets of 8, slow and controlled.
German hang, easing in: 2 holds of 20 seconds.
Straight-arm band pulldowns: 2 sets of 15, elbows locked.
Tuck front lever holds at low intensity: 3 holds of 8 seconds.
Light biceps and forearm curls: 2 sets of 15 to load the elbow before heavy straight-arm work.
protocols.see_clinician: Inner elbow pain that sharpens on straight-arm loading is common and slow to heal; get it looked at early.
